sections.h2: Contacting the Tyrrell County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The office is at 403 Main Street in Columbia, NC 27925. The mailing address is P.O. Box 449. Call (252) 796-2901 or fax (252) 796-0148.

Hours are 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, closed on holidays. Time any visit inside those hours. If you plan to mail a deed, use the post office box and phone first, so the staff can tell you what else the package needs. A call before you drive or mail anything saves a second trip.

Tyrrell County is small and rural: 3,537 residents in mid-2025 on 390.78 square miles of land, about 8.3 people per square mile. The median owned home is valued at $164,500 and 77.8% of homes are owner-occupied. With so few sales in a year, a buyer's lender or a title company will look hard at the paperwork on any parcel, so a clean record helps your sale move.

The Register of Deeds lets a property owner put the public on notice of an ownership interest. That public record protects later buyers and lenders from unknown transactions and hidden liens.

The records run from old land grants to modern deeds, maps, leases and agreements. The same counter also issues vital certificates and marriage licenses.

The office runs a Fraud Alert Notification Service. Register an email address and you get an automatic message whenever a recording looks possibly fraudulent. It is worth a few minutes if you own vacant land or a house you do not live in, since you are not at the parcel to notice anything odd.

The seller does. State law names the person transferring title as the one who pays the excise tax at the register's office, before the deed is recorded.

The statute sets a flat charge for each $500 of price or value, and any leftover amount counts as a full block. The county and the State share what comes in.

Do not estimate the dollar figure yourself. The attorney or title agent running your closing reads it off the settlement statement. If you are filing without one, the Columbia counter can help.

Recording charges are set statewide, so Tyrrell County charges what the General Statutes allow. Confirm any unusual items with the Columbia office before you send a package. Payment is due when the document is presented.

Charges that can apply to a Tyrrell County recording

A mortgage payoff produces a release, and that filing costs nothing. Ask your closer to confirm the release is recorded so the old lien clears from the public record.

Owners who inherit land here sometimes live far away. If the property came to you from a relative, ask a title company to review the chain of title before you list it or accept an offer, and keep any estate paperwork together with the deed.

A few steps make a distance sale easier: sign up for the register's fraud alert, get a clear title review, and line up a local contact who can handle the closing details. Paper mail and phone calls still work well in this county, so you do not have to depend on e-recording alone.

sections.h2: Why recording matters after you sell
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered deed gets no protection against creditors and later buyers who paid value. The deed that reaches the county office first usually ranks ahead.

If your deed is not recorded, a creditor with a claim against you, or a second buyer, could end up ahead of the purchaser. Make sure the deed is on its way to Columbia on closing day, whether through your closer or by your own delivery.

  • Ask when the recording will happen and how it will be submitted.
  • Keep proof of delivery if you mail the deed to P.O. Box 449.
  • Request the recording information once the register has filed it.

Interest rules sit in G.S. 105-360, and G.S. 105-355 explains the lien that follows the parcel. Unpaid taxes stay attached to the property, so they need to be settled at or before closing.

Tyrrell County offers six ways to pay: web portal, phone, mail, the tax office counter, a drop box in the hallway before the tax department door, and a bank's bill pay. Card payments carry a $2.50 fee or a 2.95% fee, whichever is greater, and e-check payments an added $2.00 fee. A bank's bill pay can lag by as much as seven business days, so start early.

For the current bill, tax rate and any prepayment discount, ask the Tyrrell County tax office. The Register of Deeds does not collect property taxes.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited house without a full estate
sections.html:
Sometimes it works. G.S. 28A-25-1 allows an affidavit for small estates, with caps of $20,000 in personal property after liens and $30,000 for a sole-heir surviving spouse after any spousal allowance. No personal representative petition can be pending, and 30 days must be up since the death.

File it with the superior court clerk where the person lived. The affidavit describes every tract of land the person owned. Whether you can then deed the land is a question for an attorney. Ask the clerk of court about the forms, and ask the register what must be recorded to show the heirs' authority to convey.

A cash buyer who closes as-is can skip repairs and showings, though the deed still has to be recorded and the title still has to be clear.

sections.h2: Closing day in Columbia, step by step
sections.html:
Typically the title agent or attorney collects your signed deed, confirms the payoff of any mortgage, and pays the excise tax out of your proceeds. The deed then goes to the register for filing. After the filing, ask for the book and page information so you hold proof that the transfer is on record. If a mortgage is being paid off, watch for the release as well: it costs nothing to file, and the old lender is responsible for sending it, so a quick check a few weeks later keeps the record tidy.

Handing over the keys and the proceeds does not wait on the recording in most closings, but your protection as seller depends on the deed reaching the Columbia office promptly.

sections.h2: What to bring when you record a deed
sections.html: Bring the signed, notarized deed, the payment for the recording fee, and the excise tax if you are filing yourself. Most sellers never do this personally, because the attorney or title agent handles it at closing. If you are sending the package yourself, call (252) 796-2901 first and ask what else the office needs for your document type.

faqs.q: What are the Tyrrell County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Nine to five on weekdays that are not holidays. Find the office at 403 Main Street in Columbia or call (252) 796-2901.

faqs.q: Is there a fraud alert for Tyrrell County property records?
faqs.a: Yes. The register offers a Fraud Alert Notification Service that emails you if a possibly fraudulent recording is made. Sign up through the register's website.

faqs.q: Who owes the conveyance tax in Tyrrell County?
faqs.a: The seller, before recording. Look for the figure on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: What does a basic recording cost in Tyrrell County?
faqs.a: The base charge covers the first 15 pages, with a per-page charge after that. Ask the office whether your document triggers extra charges.

faqs.q: Does the Tyrrell County register collect property taxes?
faqs.a: No. The tax office takes property tax payments and lists the ways to pay. Ask that office for your bill before closing.
